description.narrative: The objective of the Centralized Emergency Response System Project for Peru is to provide a more efficient response to emergencies, urgencies, and associated help line requests from the population of Lima Metropolitan area and Callao. The project has six components. 1. Physical Infrastructure component will finance the works for the construction of a 911 Center and all the furnishings needed to operate the 911 emergency response service in the Lima Metropolitan area and Callao. 2. Integrated Platform component will finance the necessary digital infrastructure to be housed at the 911 Center to enhance the capacity of the targeted First Response Units to effectively plan and respond to emergencies in a coordinated manner. 2.1. 911 Platform subcomponent will finance the provision and installation of necessary equipment for the 911 operators to communicate and transfer standardized and unified relevant information to the dispatchers. 2.2. Data communications equipment (Data Center) subcomponent will finance a data center with adequate backup, power systems, and cooling system for optimal performance with the necessary electrical protection. 2.3. Telecommunications networks subcomponent will finance the installation of an internal dedicated communications network within the 911 Center that will enable the transmission of data, voice, and video between the user terminals, the 911 Platform, and the data center. 3. 911 Central Response Protocols component will increase coordination between the 911 operators and the First Response Units through the development of standardized protocols. 4. Interconnection of the video cameras of National Police to the 911 Platform component will finance the acquisition of data communications equipment to interconnect the NPP video surveillance systems with the 911 Platform through a dedicated network to enable timely access to the occurrence of events and to improve the response time. 5. Use and Appropriation of 911 Platform component will (a) increase the efficiency of the emergency response system through the 5.1. Capacity Building subcomponent and (b) promote the benefits and the proper use of the 911 emergency response service, through the 5.2. Raise Awareness of the 911 Emergency Response System subcomponent. 6. Project supervision and management, and technical studies component will finance (a) support to National Telecommunications Program (PRONATEL) for project monitoring, evaluation, and supervision; (b) capacity-building activities; and (c) and the remaining technical studies needed for the final design of the 911 Center and the Integrated Platform, as well as for the implementation of the project.

The proposed project development objective is to provide a more efficient response to emergencies, urgencies, and associated help line requests from the population of Lima Metropolitan area and Callao.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I. A. 2. (a) of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower shall create and maintain, throughout Project implementation,a unit within PRONATEL (the “PIU”) with functions and responsibilities acceptable to the Bank, and staffed with adequate fiduciary,administrative and technical personnel as set forth in the Operational Manual.

Schedule 2, Section I. A. 2. (b) of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower shall not later than ninety (90) days after Effective Date,ensure that a procurement specialist is hired to work full time within the PIU, all under terms of reference acceptable to the Bank.

Schedule 2, Section I. A. 3. of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower shall establish, by no later than sixty (60) days after EffectiveDate, and thereafter operate and maintain throughout the period of implementation of Project activities, a Steering Committee (the“SC”), which committee shall have membership, functions, and competencies acceptable to the Bank as defined in the OperationalManual.

Schedule 2, Section I. B. 1 (B) of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall exercise its rights and carry out itsobligations under the Cooperation Agreement in such manner as to protect the interests of the Borrower and the Bank and toaccomplish the purposes of the Loan. Except as the Bank shall otherwise agree, the Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall not assign,amend, abrogate, waive, terminate or fail to enforce the Cooperation Agreement or any of its provisions.

Schedule 2, Section I. B. 1 (a) of the Loan Agreement. To facilitate the carrying out of the Project, the Borrower, throughPRONATEL, shall enter into an agreement with the First Response Units (the Cooperation Agreement), under terms, and conditionsacceptable to the Bank including, inter alia, the First Response Units responsibilities, in the Project in accordance with therelevant provisions of this Agreement.

Schedule 2, Section I. C.1 of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall carry out the Project in accordance withthe provisions of a manual (the Operational Manual), satisfactory to the Bank, which shall include, inter alia: (i) theorganizational structure of the Project, including the structure and terms of reference of personnel in charge of theimplementation of the Project; (ii) the structure and functions of the SC; (iii) the procedures for the carrying out, monitoringand evaluation of the Project; (iv) the indicators for Project monitoring and evaluation; (v) the Project procurement and financialmanagement requirements and procedures; and, (vi) the Project's chart of accounts and internal controls.

Schedule 2, Section I. D. 1 of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall ensure that the Project is carried out inaccordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to the Bank.

Schedule 2, Section I. D. 2 of the Loan Agreement. Without limitation upon the Covenant described in Schedule 2, Section I. D. 1 ofthe Loan Agreement, the Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Bank. To this end, the Borrower, through PRONATEL,shall ensure that: (a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP are implemented with due diligence and efficiency, and asfurther specified in the ESCP; (b) sufficient funds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP; (c) policies,procedures and qualified staff are maintained to enable it to implement the ESCP, as further specified in the ESCP; and, (d) theESCP or any provision thereof, is not amended, revised or waived, except as the Bank shall otherwise agree in writing, as specifiedin the ESCP, and the Borrower, through PRONATEL, has, thereafter, disclosed the revised ESCP. In case of any inconsistenciesbetween the ESCP and the provisions of the Loan Agreement, the provisions of the Loan Agreement shall prevail.

Schedule 2, Section I. D. 3 (a) of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall take all measures necessary on itspart to collect, compile, and furnish to the Bank through regular reports, with the frequency specified in the ESCP, and promptlyin a separate report or reports, if so requested by the Bank, information on the status of compliance with the ESCP, all suchreports in form and substance acceptable to the Bank, setting out, inter alia: (i) the status of implementation of the ESCP; (ii)conditions, if any, which interfere or threaten to interfere with the implementation of the ESCP; and, (iii) corrective andpreventive measures taken or required to be taken to address such conditions.

Schedule 2, Section I. D. 3 (b) of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall promptly notify the Bank of anyincident or accident related to or having an impact on the Project which has, or is likely to have, a significant adverse effect onthe environment, the affected communities, the public or workers, in accordance with the ESCP, the instruments referenced thereinand the Environmental and Social Standards.

Schedule 2, Section I. D. 4 of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through PRONATEL, shall maintain and publicize the availability ofa grievance mechanism, in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank, to hear and determine fairly and in good faith allcomplaints raised in relation to the Project, and take all measures necessary to implement the determinations made by suchmechanism in a manner satisfactory to the Bank.

Schedule 2, Section IV. of the Loan Agreement. The Borrower, through MTC, shall, no later than twenty (20) months from Effectivedate, or before the implementation of the 911 Platform, approve the necessary adjustments to the legal framework regardinggeolocation requirements that shall include the obligation of mobile operators to share real time data and transfer the geolocationdata to the 911 Emergency Response System.

title.narrative: 5.2. Awareness raising campaign on the proper use of the 911 emergency response service designed and launched

comment.narrative: Campaign to raise awareness among the population on the importance of the 911 emergency response service designed and launched. The campaign focuses on informing the population of the Lima Metropolitan area and Callao about the correct use of the 911 emergency response service, as well as the centralization of the emergency response services in a unique number, 911, and the future disappearance of the other numbers (105, 106, and 116). Ongoing campaigns and dissemination of 911 proper use will be scaled up once the 911 Emergency Response System is fully operational.

title.narrative: Share of people who called the 911 emergency response service and are satisfied with the service received

comment.narrative:
Share of people that called to the 911 number in the event of an emergency or urgency, or for requesting related information who are satisfied or very satisfied with the service provided by the 911 operators. This type of information has not been collected, and therefore baseline is 0. PRONATEL will study the possibility of carrying out this survey to analyze the satisfaction of the people who called the emergency response units with the service provided.
911 emergency response system (Integrated Platform) is not yet operational. Contract was signed in September 2024 and is currently under implementation, with an initial start of operations planned around October 2025 that will be scaled up the following year at the 911 Center. Once operational, this will allow to monitor and track user satisfaction and allow adjustments once the system is operational and then, fully installed at the 911 Center (works expected to start in August 2025).

title.narrative: Average duration of the connection time in an emergency, urgency, or related information request call

comment.narrative:
911 emergency response system (Integrated Platform) is not yet operational. Contract was signed in September 2024 and is currently under implementation, with an initial start of operations planned around October 2025 that will be scaled up the following year at the 911 Center.
Average the time taken by the operators (first line) to register all the data from an emergency or urgency call, categorize it, and transfer it to the dispatchers (second line of response). Although the PDO differentiates between emergency, urgency, and information request, the response to each incident will be equally fast with no differentiation between type of incident and therefore the average will be measured.

title.narrative: 2.1. Interoperable Integrated Platform deployed in the 911 center and in operation

comment.narrative:
Deployment and operation of the Integrated Platform (including the 911 Platform, the Data Center, and the telecommunications networks) interoperable with the Line 100 and First Response Units digital systems. The operation of the platform includes the performance of at least the following activities: (i) the receipt of calls to the 911 and the other emergency response numbers; (ii) the collection of data by the 911 operators following the protocols established; and, (iii) transfer of the data to the First Response Unit(s).
911 emergency response system is not yet operational. Contract was signed in September 2024 and is currently under implementation (with some modules already completed), and with an initial start of operations around October 2025 (to include geolocation features) that will be scaled up the following year at the 911 Center.

title.narrative: Reduction of malicious calls received by the Integrated Platform, out of which

The indicator metric (reduction of malicious calls) has been considered as part of the design of the 911 Platform. Decrease of the number of malicious calls received by the 911 emergency response service and Line 100, which are not considered real emergencies, urgencies, related information calls, or GBV related issues. It includes disturbing, false, mistaken, silent, and repeated calls. During the Project, the number of malicious calls is expected to decline from around 8.28 million to 4.64 million.

comment.narrative:
Number of 911 operators in charge of the reception of emergency calls and video surveillance in the emergency center trained on the use of the 911 Platform, the transfer of the calls to the First Response Units, and coordination for the follow-up of emergencies from the beginning to the closing of an emergency or urgency.
The training of 911 operators (first batch) on use of 911 Platform will start in August 2025 once the 911 Platform is under implementation and initial start of operations (October 2025) is under way.

title.narrative: 2.4 Calls transferred and handled by the GBV Line

comment.narrative:
The handling of calls is defined as the provision of orientation, information, counseling, and emotional support for people affected by domestic violence and sexual assault by Line 100 staff. The indicator measures the number of calls answered by the 911 operators and connected to the GBV Line 100 staff.
911 emergency response system is not yet operational. Contract was signed in September 2024 and is currently under implementation, with an initial start of operations around October 2025 (to include geolocation features) that will be scaled up the following year at the 911 Center.

title.narrative: 3.1. Cooperation Agreement signed between PRONATEL, the NPP, SAMU, PCVF, and Line 100

comment.narrative: To facilitate the carrying out of the project PRONATEL will sign a Cooperation Agreement with the First Response Units in Peru (the NPP, SAMU, and the PCVF), and Line 100. The Cooperation Agreement aims at facilitating at minimum the development of the protocols, interoperability between the 911 integrated platform and the systems used by the First Response Units and Line 100, and defining and implementing capacity building activities. All cooperation agreements have been signed with PRONATEL, including the one with NPP.

title.narrative: 2.3. Total effective calls made to the 911 emergency response service

comment.narrative:
Effective calls are defined as the successful calls responded to by the 911 operators. The indicator measures total number of calls made to the 911 emergency response service and Line 100 that were really seeking help from the First Response Units due to an emergency or an urgency, seeking the Line 100 services, or requesting information related to emergencies and urgencies.
911 emergency response system is not yet operational. Contract was signed in September 2024 and is currently under implementation (with some modules already completed), and with an initial start of operations around October 2025 (to include geolocation features) that will be scaled up the following year at the 911 Center.

title.narrative: 2.2. Total calls received by the 911 emergency response service, including those that are malicious and not answered

comment.narrative:
Total number of calls made to the 911 and Line 100, seeking assistance from First Response Units due to an emergency or urgency; requesting information related to an emergency or an urgency; seeking help on GBV issues; not answered, or being malicious. The decrease in the number of calls is due to the decrease in the number of malicious calls.
